[[File:ETH-BIB-Graf,_Gian_Michele_(1962-)-Portr_19583.jpg|thumb|Gian Michele Graf in 2019]]
'''Gian Michele Graf''' (born 14 July 1962) is a Swiss mathematical physicist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Gian Michele Graf|website=Institut für Theoretische Physic, ETH Zürich|url=https://itp.phys.ethz.ch/research/mathphys/graf.html}}</ref>

Graf studied physics and mathematics at [[ETH Zurich]], where he graduated in 1986 with ''[[Diplom]]'' thesis supervised by [[Jürg Fröhlich]] and received his doctorate in 1990 with thesis supervised by Walter Hunziker (1935–2012) . From 1990 to 1992 Graf was an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Caltech]]. At ETH Zurich he was from 1992 to 1998 an assistant professor and from 1998 to 2001 an associate professor and is since 2001 a full professor.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Curriculum vitae & Publication list, Gian Michele Graf|website=ETH Zürich|url=https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/phys/theoretical-physics/itp-dam/documents/graf/cve.pdf}}</ref>

He was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1996 and in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gian Michele Graf|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/gian-michele-graf}}</ref> He has been a visiting researcher in six different countries.<ref name=CV/>

Graf's research deals with fundamental thermodynamic properties of matter (especially questions related to the problem of the "stability of matter" mathematically investigated by [[Elliott Lieb]] and others<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bugliaro, Luca|author2=Fröhlich, Jürg|author3=Graf, Gian Michele|title=Stability of quantum electrodynamics with nonrelativistic matter|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=77|year=1996|issue=17 |pages=3494–3498|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3494|pmid=10062234 |bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.3494B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Fefferman, Charles|author-link=Charles Fefferman|author2=Fröhlich, Jürg|author3=Graf, Gian Michele|title=Stability of ultraviolet-cutoff quantum electrodynamics with non-relativistic matter|journal=Comm. Math. Phys.|volume=190|year=1997|issue=2 |pages=309–330|doi=10.1007/s002200050243|bibcode=1997CMaPh.190..309F |s2cid=2037788 }}</ref>), many-body scattering processes in quantum mechanics, quantum pumps and various problems of [[solid-state physics]] such as the [[quantum Hall effect]] and [[topological insulator]]s. 

He was a plenary speaker at the 10th [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]] (ICMP) in Leipzig in 1991<ref name=CV/> and an invited speaker at the 14th ICMP in Lisbon in 2003.<ref name="Jean-Claude2006">{{cite book|editor=Zambrini Jean-Claude|title=XIVth International Congress On Mathematical Physics|chapter=Transport in adiabatic quantum pumps|author=Graf, G. M.|author2=Elgart, A.|author3=Sadun, L.|author4=Schnee, K.|pages=171–178|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oObICgAAQBAJ&pg=PA171|date=7 March 2006|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4480-76-5}}</ref> In 1992 he was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Fellow]].<ref name=CV/> He was an invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in 1998 in Berlin<ref>{{cite book|author=Graf, Gian Michele|chapter=Stability of matter in classical and quantized fields|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=153–162|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011573000}}</ref> and of the ICM in 2006 in Madrid.

Graf is a Swiss ''Bürger'' of [[Lugano]] and [[Rebstein]].
